security_relationship.boundary: Privacy Shield owns privacy-specific policy, controls, status, and user-facing privacy explanations. Wardveil owns security and protection identity. Neither identity replaces the other.

adoption_model.requirement: A GoreeCloud component adopts only the Privacy Shield capabilities relevant to the data, network, telemetry, sharing, metadata, external-content, or client-surface behaviors it actually implements.

capabilities.description: Minimize collection, retention, exposure, and propagation of user or operational data beyond the component's documented purpose.
Make telemetry, analytics, diagnostics, and externally transmitted usage data explicit, bounded, reviewable, and disabled by default unless required and approved.
Reduce unnecessary metadata creation, retention, export, sharing, and cross-service correlation.
Control third-party resources, embeds, trackers, remote content, and external requests according to the consuming component's runtime capabilities.
Apply privacy-aware defaults and explicit user intent to sharing, export, link generation, synchronization, and interoperability workflows.
Prefer local processing when materially practical and privacy-preserving, and identify external processing boundaries when local execution is unavailable.
Expose understandable Privacy Shield status, active protections, limitations, exceptions, and user-controlled overrides in Glaze UI when a component has a user interface.
Provide normalized privacy-relevant events suitable for local audit, diagnostics, Manager visibility, or future platform orchestration without exposing sensitive payloads by default.

non_goals: Replacing DNS filtering with browser rules
Centralizing all application data into Privacy Shield
Forcing Browser-specific blocking semantics onto non-browser applications
